transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-05-20
- Time: 16:30 UTC (approx)
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Jasmine Patel (Redwood CSM); Priya Rao (HaloHealth Head of ML), Mark Elliott (Infra), Dana Cho (PM), Ravi Sinha (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Redwood and HaloHealth scoped a 3-week POC to validate production throughput and tail latency for a conversational triage assistant. Key outcomes: run a replay of 72h anonymized traffic against Redwood hosted + a dedicated node variant, measure p50/p95/p99 latencies and cost delta for quantized model, verify VPC private egress and KMS integration. Success criteria draft: p95 < 200ms for short queries (<64 tokens), p99 < 1s, sustained average QPS 180 with burst to 650, no data residency gaps, SOC2/SSO acceptance. Next steps: share containerized replay runner, provide traffic slice, run bench week-of 2025-05-26.

Topics covered:
- Workload portrait: QPS shapes, burst cadence, concurrency
- Token distribution: input vs output length, median/95th
- Bench design: replay vs synthetic, measurement hooks (latency percentiles, token/cost accounting)
- Deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC
- Security/compliance checklist and timeline

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Alright everyone, thanks for carving out time. We're here to scope the POC and make sure we have measurable success criteria, timing, and what to run for benchmarks. Can I get a quick round of who is on from HaloHealth?
[00:08] Priya Rao: Hi, this is Priya Rao, Head of ML. I'm leading the model side and will own the traffic artifact.
[00:12] Mark Elliott: Mark, infra. I'll handle the data export and any network/VPC questions.
[00:15] Dana Cho: Dana, product. Focused on the SLA and user-experience metrics.
[00:19] Ravi Sinha: Ravi, security. I'll review SOC2, SAML, KMS integrations.
[00:22] Sofia Martinez: Great. Liam from our SE team will walk the workload questions. Over to you Liam.
[00:26] Liam O'Connor: Thanks. Quick agenda: 1) understand current traffic shape, 2) confirm what success looks like, 3) pick bench methodology, and 4) timeline. Priya, can you describe current QPS and typical request sizes?
[00:40] Priya Rao: Sure. In prod right now we're seeing a 5-day moving avg of 180 QPS daytime peak, nighttime avg is 40. We have heavy episodic bursts when marketing campaigns hit—those bursts can ramp to ~650 qps for a few minutes and then back down. Concurrency per model instance varies, we typically see 8-12 concurrent open sessions but because of chat history KV cache growth some requests become expensive. Input tokens median around 14, mean like 28 because there are long context cases. Output tokens median 36, 95th around 420 for follow-up flows.
[01:20] Liam O'Connor: Helpful. So median input 14, median output 36, 95th output 420—good. For the POC we usually ask for a 72h slice that captures a representative burst window and some long-context threads. That lets us run a replay and produce the token distribution telemetry.
[01:38] Priya Rao: We'll do that. Quick note — some messages contain PHI, we'll need to anonymize. We'll scrub PII and replace entities.
[01:43] Mark Elliott: We'll stage an S3 bucket with the slice and pre-signed urls. Is there any particular format you want? JSONL with prompt/response pairs, plus metadata about timestamps and session ids.
[01:53] Liam O'Connor: JSONL is perfect. Include per-request model version, prompt length and response length fields if possible. If you can include the original timestamp that helps for burst reconstruction.
[02:02] Dana Cho: On success criteria: Dana here—what do you normally recommend for p95/p99 targets for a chat assistant? Our users expect snappy answers for short clarifications but longer completions can be slower.
[02:14] Jasmine Patel: From CSM perspective we'd propose p95 < 250ms for short (<64 tokens) single-turn calls and p99 < 1s overall. But we can adapt based on token mix. For the POC let's gate on p99 for the 95th token-length cohort.
[02:28] Liam O'Connor: Exactly. We typically define cohorts: short (<64 out), mid (64-256), long (>256). We'll report p50/p95/p99 per cohort, cost per 1k tokens, and tail-latency for concurrency spikes.
[02:41] Priya Rao: That cohorting works for us. Our SLA ask from product is p95 < 300ms overall under steady-state and burst handling with graceful degradation during scaled events.
[02:51] Sofia Martinez: Great, we'll include an A/B comparison: Redwood hosted default model variant vs dedicated-reserved instance with quantized model. That should show cost/latency tradeoffs.
[03:02] Ravi Sinha: On the security front, we need to validate KMS integration for key rotation and audit logs for requests. Also SAML SSO for console access and RBAC for who can see traces. Does Redwood provide per-request audit logs and retention controls?
[03:18] Liam O'Connor: Yes, we can provide request-level audit logs, and retention is configurable in the POC. KMS is supported — there's an integration for customer-managed keys in private deployments; for hosted we can offer bring-your-own-key via AWS KMS with an HSM-backed policy, we'll include details in the security doc.
[03:33] Mark Elliott: Good. For network, we want to test a VPC private egress route for sessions that have PHI. Can the POC run in a VPC or does that require a private deployment?
[03:44] Jasmine Patel: We can run a private VPC-connected POC — there are two patterns: 1) Redwood Hosted with VPC peering and private endpoints (fast), or 2) a Private deployment package (on-prem or customer VPC). For the POC, the VPC peering is usually quicker. We'll list both in the runbook.
[03:58] Priya Rao: Ok. Bench methodology question — replay vs synthetic. If we replay real traffic, do you do request timing to reproduce bursts, or do you flatten to a steady QPS?
[04:10] Liam O'Connor: We replay with original timing to reproduce bursts. There are knobs to accelerate while preserving inter-request ordering and session grouping. We also seed synthetic tails to stress test concurrency. We'll annotate which runs are "timing-accurate" and which are stress tests.
[04:24] Dana Cho: How do you measure cost? We need token accounting per request and compute cost for reserved capacity.
[04:29] Liam O'Connor: We'll capture tokens in the runner and produce a per-run cost estimate using Redwood's pricing model (we'll provide a cost calculator spreadsheet). For dedicated reserved nodes we'll estimate amortized GPU cost and effective cost-per-1k-tokens. For quantized model runs we'll show delta in latency and cost.
[04:44] Priya Rao: Any limitations on model sizes or KV cache behavior? Our LLM uses session history caching and token windows up to 8192 in some flows.
[04:53] Liam O'Connor: The runtime supports large context lengths; performance depends on seq len distribution and KV cache re-use. For very long windows we expect per-token latency to increase; we'll measure per-token throughput and show when batching helps. Also note: for 8k sequences we recommend dedicated GPU with tensor-cores and specific kernel paths — we'll include that in the model profile.
[05:12] Ravi Sinha: Auditability — we need to ensure logs are tamper-evident and have export capability to our SIEM. Is there an API for that?
[05:20] Jasmine Patel: Yes, audit logs are exportable to S3 or pushed via syslog, and there are immutable retention policies we can configure for the POC. We'll share the docs.
[05:29] Mark Elliott: Timeline — you mentioned a 3-week POC. Can you walk the milestones?
[05:33] Sofia Martinez: Week 0 (this week) — agree scope and success criteria, exchange artifacts. Week 1 — Redwood sets up replay runner and runs initial baseline on hosted; run timing-accurate replay. Week 2 — run dedicated node variant and quantized model runs; stress tests. Week 3 — joint analysis, runbook handoff, and final decision meeting. Does that align?
[05:52] Priya Rao: That aligns. We may need a short delay to scrub PHI — target to upload by Friday.
[05:58] Dana Cho: Ok, on success criteria again — will the final signoff be by product + infra + security?
[06:04] Sofia Martinez: Yes, we'll document success gates and approval owners. Typical gate: product signs off on latency and accuracy regression thresholds, infra signs off on VPC/KMS setup, security signs off on SOC2 artifacts and logability.
[06:14] Priya Rao: About accuracy regression — we do want to ensure quantization or different model variants don't exceed a small delta in our eval metric (we use top-n F1 for entity extraction). How do you track quality drift during the POC?
[06:27] Liam O'Connor: We run an eval harness on a holdout eval set and report metric deltas per model variant. We'll include that as part of the bench report so you can see latency vs accuracy trade-offs.
[06:36] Dana Cho: Any recommended thresholds?
[06:39] Jasmine Patel: Typical threshold is <1.5% absolute drop on the primary metric, but that's negotiable. We'll gate the quantized model result on that.
[06:46] Priya Rao: Good. A couple technical clarifications: when you report p95/p99 for concurrency spikes do you include queueing time, or is that pure server processing latency?
[06:55] Liam O'Connor: We surface both: end-to-end response latency from client perspective (includes network plus any queueing) and server-side processing latency. For the POC we'll highlight queueing time at high concurrency so you can see where autoscale/fallback triggers kick in.
[07:08] Mark Elliott: Autoscale? During the POC will autoscale be enabled on dedicated nodes? We want to observe scaling behavior.
[07:14] Sofia Martinez: For dedicated reserved pools we can enable controlled autoscaling with bounding rules. We'll run a test with autoscale off and another with it on to show differences in tail.
[07:23] Ravi Sinha: On data residency — we have EU customer data and require logs to be kept within EU region. Can Redwood pin the POC region?
[07:31] Liam O'Connor: Yes, region pinning for the POC is doable. We'll provision the POC infra in eu-west-1 if needed. We'll note that in the runbook.
[07:38] Priya Rao: On tokenization differences — our preprocessing uses a proprietary tokenizer which sometimes maps to different token counts than GPT tokenizers. Will that affect the cost accounting?
[07:49] Liam O'Connor: We measure tokens based on the model tokenizer used in the run. If you have a pre-tokenized stream we can consume token counts you provide, but for cost calc we normalize to Redwood's tokenizer for the chosen model. We'll document mapping and provide a reconciliation table.
[08:05] Dana Cho: Bench outputs — what will you deliver?
[08:08] Jasmine Patel: Deliverables: 1) replay-run raw CSV with per-request latency and token counts, 2) summary report with p50/p95/p99 by cohort, cost estimates, model variant comparisons, and recommended production configuration, 3) runbook for deployment and handoff, and 4) short demo call to present results.
[08:27] Priya Rao: Also include the eval comparison and any suggested guardrails for canary rollouts.
[08:31] Liam O'Connor: Absolutely. We'll provide a canary recipe (traffic split, gating rules, rollback triggers).
[08:36] Mark Elliott: One more infra point — do you support TLS mutual auth for service-to-service ingress?
[08:41] Jasmine Patel: Yes, mutual TLS is supported for private deployments and can be configured for hosted private endpoints. We'll document the steps.
[08:49] Sofia Martinez: Great. Let's talk specifics for the replay file fields — Priya, can you include: timestamp, session_id, prompt_text (anonymized), response_text (anonymized), token_in_count, token_out_count, original_model_version?
[09:01] Priya Rao: Yes we can. We'll also add a 'burst_label' field if a request is part of a campaign burst.
[09:07] Liam O'Connor: Perfect. For long-context sessions, if you can provide the context window size per request that helps us model KV cache misses vs hits.
[09:14] Priya Rao: We'll include context_window_tokens.
[09:17] Dana Cho: On KPI cutoffs — product wants to see cost per successful triage completion. How do you count success eclectically?
[09:24] Liam O'Connor: We'll instrument success as a binary field if you can provide an outcome label in the export; otherwise we'll approximate by response length and downstream action. Ideally provide a 'success_flag' in the export.
[09:33] Priya Rao: We can add that to the export.
[09:35] (brief cross talk)
[09:40] Sofia Martinez: Ok, timeline and owners recap: Sofia to send POC playbook and pricing note by Wednesday (2025-05-21). Liam to provide replay runner container and sample config by Friday (2025-05-23). Priya to upload 72h anonymized traffic by Thursday (2025-05-22). Ravi to send any special security constraints by Thursday. We will target bench week of 2025-05-26.
[10:03] Dana Cho: For scheduling, can we tentatively book Tuesday and Thursday in that week for baseline and dedicated runs?
[10:09] Jasmine Patel: We'll suggest 2 slots and lock one after we get the traffic.
[10:13] Priya Rao: Question — what happens if the 95th percentile in our long-tail is above your dedicated SLOs? Do you offer auto-fallback to smaller model?
[10:23] Liam O'Connor: Yes. We support model-fallback and routing policies. In production you can route long calls to a lower-latency/less-costly variant or stream partial responses. For the POC we'll show a fallback run to demonstrate graceful degradation.
[10:36] Mark Elliott: Any caveats about token-mix bias? If our workload is very output-heavy that will affect tail and cost.
[10:43] Liam O'Connor: Right — token-mix is the biggest driver of cost. We'll show cost-per-1k tokens and per-request costs so you can see the delta.
[10:50] Priya Rao: Ok that's all the clarifying Qs I had.
[10:54] Sofia Martinez: Great. Quick note on measurements — we'll publish a 'traffic fingerprint' (QPS histogram, token length CDF, concurrency quantiles, burst heatmap) as part of the artifact so you have a concise profile.
[11:05] Dana Cho: Love that. How do you share the results? PDF + CSV + a short video?
[11:09] Jasmine Patel: PDF summary, raw CSVs for the runs, and a short 20-min recorded walkthrough demo.
[11:14] Ravi Sinha: For security review — we need to see SOC2 Type II and encryption key handling docs before we start the replay. Is that ok?
[11:21] Sofia Martinez: Yes, we'll send SOC2 artifacts and a security checklist as part of the initial package.
[11:26] Mark Elliott: Anything else we should be aware of?
[11:30] Priya Rao: Just that some sessions have multi-party context which may change token distribution; we'll flag those.
[11:36] Sofia Martinez: Good. Let's recap next steps and owners.
